title: About
text: About I build models and the machinery that keeps them running — fine-tuning, evaluation harnesses, deployment, monitoring. My working rule is that a result only counts if it is measured against a published baseline, reported with a confidence interval, and survives a rerun. Right now that means multimodal vision-language models for surgical video, in a research collaboration between LMU Munich and ZEISS , plus self-supervised segmentation of archaeological LiDAR data. Outside the lab I work on agentic systems: tool calling, MCP, structured outputs, and how they break.

title: Surgical Vision-Language Foundation Model
text: Surgical Vision-Language Foundation Model LMU Munich × ZEISS · research collaboration · 2026 – present Built and ran a self-supervised pretraining benchmark on an ImageNet-init ViT-B/16 backbone, comparing DINO v1 against LeJEPA, then measuring zero-shot calibration and accuracy on HyperKvasir before vs. after in-domain SSL. Designed a checkpoint-resumable streaming pipeline that reads the full ~4.9M-image GastroNet-5M corpus (all 506 source archives) directly off the remote portal with no local pre-curation, handling truncated images and archive-host outages without breaking exact step-count reproducibility across SLURM resubmits. Selected the winning setting against a pre-registered rule (no regression on accuracy, balanced-accuracy, AUROC or segmentation Dice vs. the pre-SSL baseline): DINO/ImageNet passes cleanly across all 5 HyperKvasir tasks, while LeJEPA/ImageNet regresses on every classification task and on segmentation. 4.9M images × 3 epochs = 113,064 optimizer steps per setting, trained single-GPU on LRZ H100/A100. The winning checkpoint is promoted as a foundation model for downstream fine-tuning. Pretraining Results → PyTorch Lightning DINO v1 LeJEPA ImageNet ViT-B/16 Weights & Biases SLURM H100 / A100 Repository private — research collaboration. Happy to walk through the work.

title: Wildboar compensation and tolerance — statistical consulting analysis
text: Wildboar compensation and tolerance — statistical consulting analysis Statistical consulting for Mengxi Kou · LMU Munich / Carson Center · 2026 A reproducible analysis of a cleaned field survey on compensation applications, agricultural losses, policy support and tolerance toward wild boars in two Chinese counties. The project turns the full questionnaire into an auditable evidence trail, from exploratory data analysis and measurement validation through ordinal models, Bayesian checks, PLS-SEM, mediation, prediction and stress testing. The public artifact explains every analysis script line by line and reports the limits of causal interpretation, including county-period confounding, measurement overlap, structural missingness and unmeasured confounding. title: gnhf — merged fix to a 3.8k-star autonomous coding agent
text: gnhf — merged fix to a 3.8k-star autonomous coding agent Open-source contribution · August 2026 · PR #213 merged into main, shipping in v0.1.46 gnhf runs a coding agent in an unattended loop against an objective. Its --max-tokens safety cap was undercounting spend by 183x: the provider adapters report four token buckets, the orchestrator stored only two, and the budget check silently dropped cache reads and cache writes. One reported run believed it was at 22% of a 1,000,000-token budget while it had already billed 41.1M tokens and $48.64. The cap never fired. I widened orchestrator state to carry all four buckets and normalized the adapter boundary so they stay mutually exclusive — Claude was folding cache reads into inputTokens , and Codex nests cached tokens inside OpenAI's input_tokens — then threaded the corrected total through the renderer, exit summary and CLI help so the displayed numbers agree with the enforced cap. Merged through the maintainer's no-mistakes review gate after three AI review rounds, with 760 tests and 6 CI checks green. title: MONAI — per-class rank fix in EmbeddingCollapseMetric
text: MONAI — per-class rank fix in EmbeddingCollapseMetric Open-source contribution · 8.7k stars · PR #9117 · September 2026 · open, pending maintainer review MONAI's EmbeddingCollapseMetric aggregate score silently dropped a class's collapse indicator whenever that class had no valid per-class rank — so a fully collapsed minority class could stay invisible in the single summary score even though its own per-class value already flagged it. Fixed the reduction step to fold all valid per-class ranks into the aggregate, added regression tests reproducing the gap (verified they fail without the fix), and addressed maintainer review feedback with clarifying docstrings. Python PyTorch Metric design Regression testing

title: TraceForge — prompt to manufacturable circuit board
text: TraceForge — prompt to manufacturable circuit board European Hackathon League, Munich · Cognition track · August 2026 · team of five Describe a circuit in plain English and an agent designs it, checks its own electrical and design rules against live component stock, repairs what it gets wrong, and exports Gerbers a factory can build. Every view — schematic, PCB, 3D, BOM, fab files — derives from one Circuit JSON, so they cannot disagree with each other. Built in one 20-hour window. I owned the distributor-availability layer: the Mouser integration for lifecycle, stock depth and minimum order quantity, plus a web-scraping sub-agent layer so the design loop never depended on a single stock source. title: Twin — an operated, evaluated agent on this site
text: Twin — an operated, evaluated agent on this site Personal project · 2026 · live on this page: open the chat in the corner A chat assistant that answers from this portfolio, cites the section it used and scrolls the page to it, books calls on my calendar and passes on messages. A LangGraph pipeline routes each question; complex ones are split by a planner, searched in parallel and searched again where evidence is missing, with every step shown in the chat. Model calls go through a router across Gemini (EU region) and open models on Groq, and degrade to plain links rather than guess. Any action that changes something, a booking or a message, pauses for an explicit yes. Measured rather than asserted: research mode raised evidence recall from 0.685 to 0.810 on 12 multi-hop questions (+0.125, 95% CI +0.05 to +0.22) at about twice the cost, so it only runs on complex questions. A claim-verification step I built showed no benefit and is switched off. A 36-case adversarial suite, including poisoned retrieved documents, passed when last run, and five incidents are written up, among them an evaluation I discarded after provider rate limits contaminated it. title: Service Desk AI — bounded multi-agent operations desk
text: Service Desk AI — bounded multi-agent operations desk Personal project · 2026 · full stack, runs with one command An enterprise service desk where a front router receives a request, retrieves policy evidence with citations, and delegates to a bounded ERP, CRM, HR or scheduling specialist. The model classifies and drafts; trusted Python code validates its output, picks the only permitted tools, and holds every protected write behind an IT approval step. The model never sees raw records, never chooses an arbitrary tool and never executes a mutation. Unavailable, malformed, unsafe or low-confidence output falls through to human review by design, not by accident. title: AI Agent Security — multi-step tool attacks
text: AI Agent Security — multi-step tool attacks Kaggle Featured competition hosted by OpenAI / Google / IEEE Python harnesses and prompt suites that drive tool-using agents (GPT-OSS, Gemma) through adversarial multi-step scenarios. The deliverable is not a clever one-off jailbreak: it is a reproducible failure — one that survives a rerun, has an isolated cause in the tool-calling or context-handling path, and can be turned into a regression test. title: EdgeLoop — ML from training set to device firmware
text: EdgeLoop — ML from training set to device firmware Personal project · 2026 · full stack, runs with one command The whole path a model takes to reach an IoT device: synthetic building telemetry, a trainer with a fixed seed, a checksummed JSON artifact, C firmware constants generated from it, and dependency-free inference running on the device. The cloud is a fleet-management and observability layer — it never needs the raw samples to know a device found a problem. The same inference contract implemented twice, in Python and in C, with the artifact checksum verified before use. Telemetry ingestion is idempotent and deployments are audited.
